intended_object: Let R be a ring that is complete for the I-adic topology, and F an R-linear endomorphism of R[X_σ]. The object is the unique continuous R-linear extension of F to the ring of restricted power series R{X_σ}, i.e. the series whose coefficients tend to 0 I-adically. This ring is the I-adic completion of R[X_σ]. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the uniqueness and polynomial-agreement lemmas that follow.
explanation:
Construction. An R-linear F automatically maps I^n·R[X] into itself, so it reduces to a linear map F_n on (R/I^n)[X] (`polynomialLinearMapMod`). These maps commute with the transition maps.

For a restricted series f, the definition takes its reductions f mod I^n, applies F_n to each, and glues the results into an element of the inverse limit. It then pulls that element back to restricted series through the library's ring isomorphism R{X} ≅ AdicCompletion(I·R[X]) R[X]. This is exactly the standard continuous, I-adically convergent extension f = Σ a_α X^α ↦ Σ a_α F(X^α).

Supporting lemmas. `restrictedLinearExtension_polynomial` shows the map agrees with F on polynomials. `restrictedLinearExtension_unique` shows it is the unique such map that preserves the reduction kernels. Additivity and R-linearity are proved, not assumed.

Hypotheses. Completeness of R is genuinely needed: without it, Σ a_α F(X^α) need not converge in R{X}, and the identification with the completion fails. A general σ and any commutative ring R are allowed, so the setting is not too narrow.

Mathlib comparison. Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.map` gives the same functorial extension on the abstract completion. This definition is its concrete counterpart on the restricted power series subring, which is the intended object.
